jobs.description:
Overview

Tonal is looking for a passionate, fitness-minded Associate to join our Strategy & Corporate Development team. This role sits at the intersection of long-term strategic planning, partnerships, and high-priority business analysis. You'll work directly with senior leadership and on initiatives that shape the direction of the company, from market expansion and competitive positioning to partnership evaluation and new business opportunities.

The ideal candidate is a strong, independent, strategic thinker, highly analytical, a great team player, and comfortable operating with a great work ethic. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves quickly, and wants to go deep on the business.



What You Will Do

Strategic Planning & Market Analysis

 - Assist in data- and research-driven strategic initiatives to develop Tonal's short- and long-term strategy.

 - Synthesize and analyze quantitative and qualitative research and data sets into insights, hypotheses, implications, and recommendations.

 - Conduct market and competitive research across consumer hardware, fitness, wellness, and adjacent tech, to inform executive-level strategy discussions.

Financial Modeling & Deal Evaluation

 - Build financial models and business cases to evaluate strategic options, new market opportunities, and investment decisions.

 - Synthesize and analyze quantitative & qualitative research and data sets into insights and/or hypotheses that support initiatives, implications and/or recommendations

 - Create key analyses and negotiation support, working closely with internal and external partners to structure and execute transactions.

Partnerships & Corporate Development

 - Support strategic partnership processes end-to-end: sourcing, evaluation, financial modeling, and internal recommendation materials.

 - Partner on a range of projects spanning product development, product pricing, evaluation of new revenue opportunities, and identification of acquisition/investment targets.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Executive Communication

 - Work cross-functionally with Finance, Product, Revenue, Operations and other teams to develop and pressure-test strategic frameworks.

 - Projects could range from partnering on product development, product pricing, evaluation of new revenue opportunities, and identifying acquisition/investment targets

 - Assist in framing and communicating key conclusions, including board materials, executive presentations, and strategic memos.



Who You Are

 - 3+ years of experience in a highly analytical and strategic role (investment banking, private equity, growth equity, management consulting, corporate strategy, or corporate development).

 - Proficient in financial modeling, valuation and financial analysis

 - Demonstrated experience solving complex, ambiguous, and analytically challenging problems.

 - Excellent verbal and written communicator, able to distill complex analysis into clear, executive-ready narratives.

 - Self-starter who excels in a fast-paced, resource-constrained, and fluid environment. You figure things out rather than wait for direction.

 - Willingness to step up to greater responsibility and take ownership of projects, strong desire to contribute to overall goals

 - Passionate about fitness and wellness. Genuine curiosity about Tonal's business and the broader consumer, fitness, and tech landscape.

 - Strong stakeholder management skills and comfort working directly with senior leadership.

 - Bachelor's degree required; top academic record preferred.



Skills Preferred

 - Proficient in financial modeling, valuation, and financial analysis (three-statement models, DCF, scenario analysis, unit economics).

 - Experience manipulating and deriving insights from data sets using tools such as Excel, Looker, or DataBricks.

jobs.description: At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of the Top 100 Inspiring Workplaces . We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more. Ready to join us?   Your Role Cloud and software are among the largest investments we make, and for every dollar there is one that could also be going toward the product itself or the team building it. Our FinOps practice exists to make sure that spend is understood, accountable, and every dollar is working as efficiently as it can. On our team, you'll help own that picture. You'll allocate spend back to the services and teams driving it, forecast where it's headed, and consult teams on best practices to propose changes that maximize efficiency. You'll be a trusted partner to product and leadership on the real cost of what we build and what's on the roadmap, helping put those dollars to better use. We're hiring across experience levels, and your scope will grow with yours: you'll build, maintain, and improve our models and automation, and lead larger initiatives as you gain experience. As a FinOps Analyst, you’ll: Forecast and get ahead of cost. You'll build and maintain the models that track, allocate, and predict where our cloud and software spend is going, monitor AWS and the rest of our stack for anomalies, and action them the moment they surface. When something breaks, you won't just put out the fire, you'll help build the guardrails that keep it from starting again.  Turn spend into decisions leadership can act on. You'll maintain and improve the chargeback model that ties every dollar back to the service, squad, or contract that incurred it, and partner with Accounting and FP&A to keep the numbers aligned. When leaders have a question about cost, you're a trusted resource they come to. Automate anything worth doing twice. You'll use Python and SQL to take manual work off the team's plate, and work with GitHub Actions, Lambda, and DBT against our data warehouse. You'll also help manage AWS reservations and Savings Plans, and we'll teach you any tools that are new to you. If a task repeats, it's a candidate for automation, and you're the one who builds it. Find the work, then drive it home. You'll spot cost and efficiency opportunities, shape them into a pitch with support from teammates and stakeholders, and once approved, help carry them across engineering, product, finance, and accounting to completion. You're the connective tissue that keeps it all moving. Location Time spent collaborating with other Hudlies in-office will be a regular part of how you work. jobs.title: Change Management Consultant (Contract)
jobs.description:
Tonal is seeking a contract Change Management Consultant to drive organization transformation for the launch of a new business line, impacting processes across the whole company. This person maps how new processes, systems, and roles ripple across functions, identifies which teams and behaviors must change, and drives the readiness work so each team operates the new way on day one.

The role brings a risk-management lens, and its primary value is cross-functional impact visibility: surfacing second-order effects that individual teams are not positioned to see, such as how a Sales process change lands on Care/Support, Finance, or Operations/Fulfillment. The consultant partners with Program Management roles and reports to Business Operations.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


1. CROSS-FUNCTIONAL IMPACT & RISK ANALYSIS

 - Build and maintain an enterprise change impact map: which teams, roles, processes, systems, and policies change because of the new business line, and how much.

 - Trace second-order effects across team boundaries, such as where one team's new process creates new work, handoffs, or failure points for another. Flag operational risks arising from the change, and solution mitigations with owners.

 - Working through functional leads, identify cross-team gaps and dependencies that teams have not surfaced themselves.

 - Translate impact into a clear "what changes for you" view per function, at both leader and frontline level.

 - Escalate cross-team conflicts and unowned gaps with a recommended resolution.


2. CHANGE MANAGEMENT, READINESS AND ADOPTION

 - Define the specific behaviors that must start, stop, or change per team, and the incentives, tools, or controls that reinforce them.

 - Partner with process owners to confirm new processes, roles, and handoffs are documented, owned, and understood.

 - Identify resistance hotspots and build targeted plans with the leaders who own them.

 - Design and run business readiness criteria and go/no-go checkpoints for each function ahead of launch milestones.

 - Develop the change, communications, and enablement plan, coordinating with functional leads.


3. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT AND REPORTING

 - Define adoption metrics and track them through launch and hypercare (for example, process compliance, error rates, ticket volume, time to proficiency).

 - Coach executive sponsors and functional leaders on their role in visibly leading the change.

 - Provide a regular readiness and impact readout to Senior Leadership Team.

 - Hand off playbooks, impact maps, and sustainment plans so internal teams own the change after the contract ends.


SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

No function surprised at launch; every material process change has a named owner; readiness criteria met by launch date; adoption metrics on target within 60 days of launch.




QUALIFICATIONS


REQUIRED

 - 7+ years in organizational change management, business readiness, or transformation consulting.

 - Led change for three or more new business line launches, market entries, or operating-model changes, each touching 5+ functions, at least one end to end as the change lead.

 - Proven change impact assessment and stakeholder analysis across Sales, Operations, Care, Finance,  Product, and cross-functional teams.

 - Expert in application of structured change methodologies (Prosci ADKAR, Kotter, or equivalent), able to adapt them to the business.

 - Strong written synthesis: turns messy cross-team inputs into one-page impact and readiness views.


PREFERRED

 - Prosci Certified Change Practitioner or ACMP CCMP.

 - Background in consumer hardware, connected fitness, subscription, or DTC/retail.

 - Experience with operational risk frameworks or launch risk registers.

 - Comfort with Jira, Confluence, Coda, or similar program tooling.
